page: Microsoft Azure E4as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at up to 3.525 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs spread across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It delivers 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware platform includes x86_64 architectural extensions such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. This instance type contains no integrated GPUs and includes no local instance storage, requiring remote storage solutions for operational disk requirements.

Performance benchmark testing indicates a clear division between single-thread capacity and aggregate parallel execution. In stress-ng single-core tests, the AMD processor achieves a strong score of 2701.99, placing it in the top 25%. However, due to its modest 4-vCPU allocation, aggregate multi-threaded metrics rank in the lower performance quartiles, as seen in stress-ng multi-core (5401.35) and Geekbench multi-core (3171.0). Memory subsystems exhibit average overall PassMark memory performance (1944.02), though raw uncached bandwidth remains moderate, measured at 36.97 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 22.23 GB/sec for write operations.

Application-level throughput reflects these resource limits. In-memory caching benchmarks report 4.21 million Redis SET operations per second, and static web serving achieves 4.88 GB/sec. Lightweight AI inference with small 135M parameter models manages 119.29 tokens per second for text generation, but drops to 6.29 tokens per second for 7B models, illustrating the limitations of CPU-bound machine learning without dedicated accelerators.

With its generous 1:8 core-to-memory allocation, the E4as_v5 offers favorable resource efficiency for workloads that require substantial memory footprint without consuming excessive processor cores. It is technically matched for intermediate relational database servers, enterprise in-memory caches, light ETL tasks, and memory-constrained microservices, provided remote storage configurations meet the necessary I/O requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure E4as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores from an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, it features an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, 32 MB of L3 cache, and standard cryptographic and vector instruction sets (AVX, AES, SHA-NI), but omits local storage and dedicated GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU throughput (stress-ng score of 2701.99), alongside average decompression and text processing capabilities, though multi-core computing and memory bandwidth fall into lower percentiles due to core count constraints. The instance delivers 4.21 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.88 GB/sec web serving throughput. It is well configured for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, and enterprise backend services that prioritize memory capacity over parallel processing power.
